questions.question: Mountain is to Valley as Peak is to _______ ?
questions.solution:

Similarly, a **Peak** (high point of a wave) is the opposite of a **Trough** (low point of a wave).

Option 3 (Apex) is incorrect — it means the highest point, again a synonym.

Option 4 (Summit) is incorrect — it also means the highest point, a synonym rather than an opposite.

Thus, the word that best completes the opposite-pair analogy is **Trough**.

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 2".

**Calculation:**

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**General Anil Chauhan**__

**__Key Points__**
__

• **General Anil Chauhan** was appointed as India's second **Chief of Defence Staff (CDS)** on **September 28, 2022**.

• The post of CDS had been vacant for nine months following the tragic death of the first CDS, **General Bipin Rawat**, in a helicopter crash in **December 2021**.

• General Chauhan is a retired officer of the **Indian Army** and had previously served as the **Eastern Army Commander** before his retirement in May 2021.

• As the CDS, he also functions as the **Secretary to the Government of India**, Department of Military Affairs, and the **Permanent Chairman of the Chiefs of Staff Committee**.

• The **Chief of Defence Staff (CDS)** is a **four-star General** rank officer who acts as the **Principal Military Adviser** to the Minister of Defence on all tri-service matters.

• The creation of the CDS post was recommended by the **Kargil Review Committee** in 2001 to improve **jointness** and **integration** between the Army, Navy, and Air Force.

• The CDS does not exercise any military command, including over the three Service Chiefs, but coordinates the functioning of the three services to ensure **synergy** in operations and procurement.

questions.question: Which of the following statement is TRUE about the Bharatiya Sakshya Sanhita?

options.text: It allows digital evidence as primary evidence.
It replaces the Code of Criminal Procedure.
It limits the use of electronic records.
It only applies to civil cases.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It allows digital evidence as primary evidence.**__

**__Key Points__**
__

• The **Bharatiya Sakshya Sanhita (BSS)** was enacted to replace the colonial-era **Indian Evidence Act, 1872**.

• One of the most transformative features of the BSS is that it treats **electronic or digital records** as **primary evidence**. This means that information stored in digital form is legally equivalent to a physical paper document.

• The scope of **documentary evidence** has been widened to include **emails, server logs, computer output, messages, and location data** stored on digital devices like smartphones and laptops.

• **Option 2 is incorrect** because the **Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS)** is the law that replaces the **Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)**, not the BSS.

• **Option 3 is incorrect** because the BSS **expands** the use of electronic records to keep pace with modern technology, rather than limiting them.

• **Option 4 is incorrect** because the BSS applies to **all judicial proceedings**, which encompasses both **civil and criminal** cases.

**Additional Information__**

• The **Bharatiya Sakshya Sanhita, 2023** received the **President's assent** on **December 25, 2023**, and officially came into effect on **July 1, 2024**.

• The new Act contains **170 sections**, which is a slight increase from the 167 sections in the original 1872 Act.

• It introduces updated provisions for the **admissibility of electronic records**, requiring a specific **certificate** to verify the authenticity and integrity of the digital source.

• The primary objective of the BSS is to **modernize the rules of evidence** and ensure that the legal system can effectively handle **cybercrimes** and digital footprints in the 21st century.

• The **Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS)** is the third major law in this overhaul, replacing the **Indian Penal Code (IPC)**.
</ul

questions.question: Which Indian satellite provides high-resolution images for monitoring agriculture, forestry, and coastal resources?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Cartosat-3**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Cartosat-3** is a third-generation agile satellite with very high-resolution imaging capabilities, designed to meet the increasing demands for **large-scale mapping**, **urban planning**, and **infrastructure development**. It is specifically optimized for monitoring **agriculture, forestry, and coastal resources**. *Hence, the correct answer is **Cartosat-3**.*
 
• Launched on **November 27, 2019**, by the **Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO)**, it was carried by the **PSLV-C47** rocket from the **Satish Dhawan Space Centre** in **Sriharikota**, **Andhra Pradesh**.
 
• The satellite boasts a **Panchromatic resolution** of **0.25 meters**, which was the highest for any civilian satellite at its launch, and a **Multispectral resolution** of **1.13 meters**.
 
• **RISAT-2** (Radar Imaging Satellite-2) was launched in **2009** and uses **Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR)** technology. It is primarily used for **defense surveillance** and disaster management as it can provide images in all weather conditions, including through clouds and at night. *Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.*
 
• **GSAT-6** is a **multimedia communication satellite** launched in **2015**. It features a large **6-meter S-band unfurlable antenna** and is used for **strategic communication** and mobile satellite services. *Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.*
 
• **INSAT-4B** was launched in **2007** as part of the **INSAT-4** series. It is a **communication satellite** equipped with **Ku-band** and **C-band** transponders, primarily serving **Direct-to-Home (DTH)** television and broadcasting needs. *Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• The **Cartosat series** is a significant part of the **Indian Remote Sensing (IRS)** satellite program. These satellites are placed in **Sun-synchronous polar orbits** to ensure consistent lighting conditions for imaging.
 
• **Remote Sensing** technology in India is used for diverse applications such as **groundwater prospecting**, **crop acreage estimation**, **flood mapping**, and **potential fishing zone (PFZ)** identification.
 
• The **National Remote Sensing Centre (NRSC)**, located in **Hyderabad**, is responsible for the acquisition, processing, and distribution of data from these satellites.
 
• **ISRO**, established on **August 15, 1969**, is the primary space agency of India, headquartered in **Bengaluru**. It operates under the **Department of Space**.
 
• The **Bhuvan** geoportal is an **ISRO** initiative that provides 2D and 3D visualization of the **Indian terrain** using high-resolution data from the **Cartosat** and **Resourcesat** series.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Cartosat-3** has a mission life of **5 years** and carries advanced sensors that operate in the **visible and near-infrared** regions of the electromagnetic spectrum.
 
• The **PSLV (Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle)** is known as the **Workhorse of ISRO** due to its high success rate in launching remote sensing satellites into polar orbits.
 
• During the **PSLV-C47** mission, **Cartosat-3** was launched along with **13 commercial nanosatellites** from the **United States of America**, highlighting India's growing role in the **global space market**.
 
• The data provided by **Cartosat-3** is crucial for **cadastral mapping**, which involves the detailed recording of property boundaries and land ownership for **governance** and **taxation**.

questions.question: What is the main objective of the 'Genome India Project'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Map genetic diversity of Indians**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
__

• The **Genome India Project (GIP)** is a national mission launched by the **Department of Biotechnology (DBT)**, Ministry of Science and Technology, to sequence the whole genomes of the Indian population.

• The primary objective is to create a **comprehensive database** of genetic variations by mapping the **genetic diversity** of India's vast and diverse population, which consists of over **4,600 distinct groups**.

• By sequencing **10,000 genetic samples** from citizens across the country, the project aims to build a **'reference genome'** specific to Indians, which will help in understanding the nature of diseases at a genetic level.

• This project is crucial because most existing global genetic databases are based on **Caucasian populations**, which do not accurately represent the unique genetic makeup of the Indian subcontinent.

• The mapping helps in identifying **genetic predispositions** to various diseases like diabetes, cardiovascular disorders, and rare genetic conditions, enabling the development of **Precision Medicine**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• The project involves a collaboration of **20 premier institutions** across India, led by the **Centre for Brain Research** at the **Indian Institute of Science (IISc)**, Bengaluru.

• In **March 2024**, the Government of India announced the successful **completion** of sequencing 10,000 genomes under this project.

• The initiative is inspired by the **Human Genome Project (HGP)**, an international scientific research project that mapped the entire human genome between 1990 and 2003.

• India is often referred to as the **world's largest genetic laboratory** due to its history of **endogamy** (marrying within the same community), which has preserved specific genetic traits and mutations within different groups.
</ul

questions.question:
Fill in the blank:
Direct taxes are collected by the government from ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Individuals and companies**__.

**__Key Points__**
__

• **Direct taxes** are defined as taxes that are paid directly to the **government** by the person or organization on whom they are levied. In this system, the **tax liability** and the **tax burden** fall on the same entity, meaning the tax cannot be shifted to another person.

• **Individuals** are a primary source of direct tax collection through **Income Tax**. Every individual whose income exceeds the basic **exemption limit** is required to pay tax to the **Central Government**. **Hence, this part of the option is correct.**

• **Companies** (both domestic and foreign) contribute to direct taxes through **Corporate Tax**. This tax is calculated on the **net profit** earned by the company during a **financial year**. **Hence, this part of the option is correct.**

• **Importers** are generally associated with **Customs Duty**, which is an **indirect tax**. The burden of customs duty is usually passed on to the end consumer by including it in the price of the imported goods. **Hence, option 2 is incorrect.**

• **Consumers** primarily pay **indirect taxes** such as **Goods and Services Tax (GST)** or **Value Added Tax (VAT)**. While they bear the ultimate burden, they do not pay it directly to the government; instead, it is collected by **traders** or service providers. **Hence, option 3 is incorrect.**

• **Traders** act as intermediaries who collect **indirect taxes** from consumers and remit them to the government. questions.question: Which organization publishes the Ease of Doing Business (EODB) report?

questions.question: Who introduced the Ryotwari System in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Thomas Munro**__.

**__Key Points__**

__

• The **Ryotwari System** was a land revenue system in **British India**, introduced to establish a direct relationship between the government and the cultivators. It was primarily introduced by **Sir Thomas Munro** and **Captain Alexander Read** at the end of the **18th century**.

• **Thomas Munro**, who served as the **Governor of Madras** from **1820 to 1827**, is credited with the formal implementation of this system across the **Madras Presidency** in **1820**. Hence, the correct answer is **Thomas Munro**.

• The system was first trialed by **Captain Alexander Read** in the **Baramahal** region (modern-day **Tamil Nadu**) in **1792** after the **Third Anglo-Mysore War**.

• Under the **Ryotwari** settlement, the **Ryots** (peasants) were recognized as the individual owners of the land. They had the right to sell, mortgage, or transfer the land as long as they paid the fixed revenue to the **East India Company**.

• Unlike the **Zamindari System**, there were no middlemen or intermediaries involved. The revenue was collected directly by **British** officials, and the rates were revised periodically, usually every **20 to 30 years**, based on soil fertility and crop type.

**Additional Information__**

__

• **Lord Cornwallis**: He is famous for introducing the **Permanent Settlement** (also known as the **Zamindari System**) in **Bengal**, **Bihar**, and **Odisha** in **1793**. In this system, **Zamindars** were made hereditary owners of the land, and the revenue amount was fixed permanently.

• **Warren Hastings**: He was the first **Governor-General of Bengal** (**1773–1785**). He introduced the **Ijaradari System** in **1772**, which involved auctioning the right to collect land revenue to the highest bidder for a period of **five years**.

• **Robert Clive**: He served as the **Governor of Bengal** twice and established the **Dual Government** system in **1765** after the **Battle of Buxar**. Under this, the **Nawab** held the **Nizamat** (administrative) powers, while the **British** held the **Diwani** (revenue collection) rights.

• **Mahalwari System**: This was another major land revenue system introduced by **Holt Mackenzie** in **1822**. It was implemented in the **North-Western Provinces**, **Punjab**, and parts of **Central India**, where the unit of revenue assessment was the village or **Mahal**.

**Important Points__**

• **Geographical Coverage**: The **Ryotwari System** covered approximately **51%** of the territory under **British** rule, including the **Madras Presidency**, **Bombay Presidency**, **Assam**, and **Coorg**.

• **Revenue Rates**: The revenue demand was exceptionally high, often reaching **50%** for dry lands and **60%** for irrigated lands. This high demand often led to the exploitation of peasants by **moneylenders** when they could not meet the **British** demands.

• **Economic Impact**: While the system aimed to protect the **Ryots** from **Zamindars**, the rigid collection methods and high taxes resulted in large-scale rural indebtedness and land alienation, as **British** officials were often more oppressive than the former intermediaries.

• **Legal Status**: The **Ryot** was considered the proprietor of the land, but this ownership was conditional. Failure to pay the tax resulted in immediate eviction by the **Government**.

questions.question: Which of the following topics falls under the State List as per the Seventh Schedule of the Constitution of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Police and public order**__.

**__Key Points__**
__

• **Article 246** of the **Constitution of India** distributes the legislative powers between the **Union** and the **States** through the **Seventh Schedule**, which contains three distinct lists.

• **Police and public order** are subjects specifically mentioned under the **State List** (List II). **Public Order** is listed as **Entry 1** and **Police** (including railway and village police) is listed as **Entry 2**. This means the **State Government** has the exclusive power to legislate on these matters. *Hence, statement 4 is correct.*

• **Defense and Armed Forces** of the Union, including the preparation for defense and all such acts as may be conducive in times of war, fall under **Entry 1** of the **Union List** (List I). Only the **Parliament** can make laws regarding the **military**, **naval**, and **air forces**. *Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.*

• **Foreign affairs and international treaties**, including all matters which bring the **Union** into relation with any **foreign country**, are covered under **Entries 10 to 14** of the **Union List**. This ensures a unified **foreign policy** for the **nation**. *Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.*

• **Currency, coinage, and legal tender**; foreign exchange and the **Reserve Bank of India** are subjects under **Entry 36** of the **Union List**. This allows the **Central Government** to maintain a uniform **monetary system** across the **country**. *Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.*

**Additional Information__**
__

• The **Union List** (List I) consists of subjects of **national importance**. It originally contained **97 subjects**, but currently, it has **100 subjects**. Major entries include **Atomic Energy**, **Railways**, **Post and Telegraph**, **Banking**, and **Census**.

• The **State List** (List II) comprises subjects of **local or regional importance**. It originally had **66 subjects**, but after various amendments, it now contains **61 subjects**. Key entries include **Agriculture**, **Public Health**, **Sanitation**, **Local Government**, **Fisheries**, and **Markets**.

• The **Concurrent List** (List III) includes subjects where both the **Parliament** and **State Legislatures** can legislate. It has **52 subjects** (originally **47**). In case of a conflict between a **Central law** and a **State law** on a concurrent subject, the **Central law** generally prevails. Examples include **Education**, **Forests**, **Marriage and Divorce**, and **Trade Unions**.

• The **42nd Amendment Act, 1976** was a landmark legislation that transferred five subjects from the **State List** to the **Concurrent List**: **Education**, **Forests**, **Weights and Measures**, **Protection of Wild Animals and Birds**, and **Administration of Justice**.

• **Residuary Powers** refer to the power to legislate on any matter not enumerated in any of the three lists. According to **Article 248**, these powers are exclusively vested in the **Parliament of India**.

**Important Points__**

• Although **Police** is a **State subject**, the **Union Government** maintains several **Central Armed Police Forces (CAPF)** such as the **Border Security Force (BSF)**, **Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF)**, and **Indo-Tibetan Border Police (ITBP)** to assist states in maintaining **internal security** and guarding **borders**.

• In certain **Union Territories** like **Delhi**, the legislative and executive power over **Police**, **Public Order**, and **Land** is reserved for the **Central Government** (Ministry of Home Affairs) under **Article 239AA** of the **Constitution**.

• The **Sarkaria Commission** (established in **1983**) and the **Punchhi Commission** (established in **2007**) were appointed to examine **Centre-State relations** and suggested that the **Seventh Schedule** should be periodically reviewed to ensure it reflects the changing **socio-economic** needs of the **country**.

• The **Seventh Schedule** is a key feature of **Indian Federalism**, ensuring a clear **division of powers** to prevent **administrative** overlaps and conflicts between different levels of **government**.
</ul

questions.question: The basic notes in Indian classical music are called ________
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Swaras**__.

**__Key Points__**
__

• **Swaras** are the fundamental musical notes in **Indian classical music**. They represent the basic pitch and are the primary units from which melodies are constructed. ***Hence, the correct answer is Swaras.***

• There are **seven** basic notes in the Indian musical scale, collectively referred to as the **Sapta Swara**. These are **Shadja (Sa)**, **Rishabha (Re)**, **Gandhara (Ga)**, **Madhyama (Ma)**, **Panchama (Pa)**, **Dhaivata (Dha)**, and **Nishada (Ni)**.

• **Ragas** are melodic frameworks or modes used for composition and improvisation. A **Raga** is not a single note but a specific combination of **swaras** that evokes a particular emotion or mood. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***

• **Talas** refer to the rhythmic cycles or time measures in **Indian music**. They provide the beat and tempo for a performance, ensuring rhythmic consistency and structure. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***

• **Alankars** are musical ornaments or sequential patterns of **swaras**. They are used to decorate a melody and demonstrate a musician's technical skill through various permutations and combinations of notes. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

**Additional Information__**
__

• **Indian Classical Music** is categorized into two major systems: **Hindustani Classical Music** of **North India** and **Carnatic Classical Music** of **South India**. Both systems use the same **seven** basic **swaras**.

• The **Sama Veda** is considered the source of **Indian music**, as it consists of verses from the **Rig Veda** set to musical notes, forming the earliest known musical tradition in **India**.

• The **Natyashastra**, an ancient encyclopedic treatise on the performing arts by **Bharata Muni** (composed between **200 BCE** and **200 CE**), provides the earliest detailed description of **swaras** and **shrutis**.

• An octave in **Indian music** is divided into **22 Shrutis** (microtones). The **seven** main **swaras** are placed at specific intervals within these **22 shrutis** to create a scale.

• The **12 notes** in a full scale consist of **7 Shuddha Swaras** (natural notes) and **5 Vikrit Swaras** (modified notes). The **Vikrit Swaras** include **4 Komal** (flat) notes and **1 Teevra** (sharp) note.

**Important Points__**

• **Achala Swaras**: These are 'immovable' or fixed notes. **Shadja (Sa)** and **Panchama (Pa)** are the only two notes that do not have **Komal** or **Teevra** variations in the **Indian musical scale**.

• **Chala Swaras**: These are 'movable' notes that can be altered from their natural positions. **Re, Ga, Ma, Dha,** and **Ni** fall into this category and can be shifted to become **Komal** or **Teevra**.

• **Vadi and Samvadi**: The **Vadi** is the most prominent note in a **Raga**, often called the 'king' of the raga, while the **Samvadi** is the second most important note, acting as the 'minister' to support the melody.

• **Aroha and Avroha**: **Aroha** is the ascending sequence of **swaras** (e.g., **Sa Re Ga Ma Pa Dha Ni Sa**), and **Avroha** is the descending sequence (e.g., **Sa Ni Dha Pa Ma Ga Re Sa**).
</ul

questions.question: Which Mughal emperor introduced the Charbagh style of gardens?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Babur**__.

**__Key Points__**

• **Babur**, the founder of the **Mughal Empire** in India, is credited with introducing the **Charbagh** style of gardening to the Indian subcontinent. He reigned from **1526 to 1530**.

questions.question: Which piece moves in an 'L' shape in chess?
questions.solution:

__

• The **Knight** is the specific chess piece that moves in an **'L' shape**. This movement is defined as moving **two squares** in a straight line (either vertically or horizontally) and then **one square** perpendicular to that line. ***Hence, the Knight is the correct answer.***

• A unique characteristic of the **Knight** is its ability to **jump over** other pieces. No other piece on the board, including the **Queen** or **Rook**, can move past a square occupied by another piece. This makes the Knight exceptionally valuable in **closed positions** where the board is crowded with pawns.

• The **Rook** moves in straight lines along **ranks** (rows) and **files** (columns) for any number of unoccupied squares. It cannot move diagonally or in an 'L' shape, and it is blocked by other pieces. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***

• The **Bishop** moves any number of squares in a **diagonal** direction. Each player starts with two Bishops, one restricted to **light squares** and the other to **dark squares** throughout the entire match. They cannot move in an 'L' shape. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***

• The **Queen** is the most powerful piece on the board, combining the movements of the **Rook** and the **Bishop**. While it can move any number of squares vertically, horizontally, or diagonally, it lacks the **'L' shape** jumping capability of the Knight. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

**Additional Information__**
__

• **Chessboard Layout**: The game is played on a square board divided into an **8x8 grid** containing **64 squares**. The squares alternate between **light** and **dark** colors, and the board is positioned so that each player has a light square on their bottom-right corner.

The earliest known form was **Chaturanga**, which featured pieces representing the four divisions of the military: infantry, cavalry, elephants, and chariots.

• **Piece Valuation**: In standard chess theory, pieces are assigned numerical values to help players evaluate positions. A **Pawn** is worth **1 point**, **Knights** and **Bishops** are worth **3 points** each, **Rooks** are worth **5 points**, and the **Queen** is worth **9 points**.

• **FIDE**: The **International Chess Federation** (Fédération Internationale des Échecs) is the global body that governs chess. Founded in **1924** in **Paris**, **France**, it organizes the **World Chess Championship** and awards titles like **Grandmaster**.

• **World Champions**: The first official **World Chess Championship** was held in **1886**, won by **Wilhelm Steinitz**. Since then, the title has been held by legendary players such as **Bobby Fischer**, **Garry Kasparov**, and **Magnus Carlsen**.

• **Stalemate**: This is a situation where the player whose turn it is has no legal moves and their **King** is not in check. A **Stalemate** results in an immediate **draw**, regardless of the material advantage on the board.

__

• In **Option 2**, **China** is a permanent member, but **India** is not. **India** is a member of the **G4 nations** and has been actively seeking a permanent seat on the **Security Council** for several years. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***

• In **Option 4**, neither **India** nor **South Africa** are permanent members of the **UNSC**. Both countries are significant regional powers that advocate for **UNSC reforms** to include more representation from the **Global South**. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

**Additional Information__**
__

• The **Permanent Members (P5)** of the **UNSC** possess the **Veto Power**, which allows any one of them to prevent the adoption of any 'substantive' resolution. This power was established at the **founding of the United Nations** in **1945** following **World War II**.

• **Russia's** seat was originally held by the **Union of Soviet Socialist Republics (USSR)**. After the **dissolution of the Soviet Union** in **December 1991**, the **Russian Federation** was recognized as its legal successor state in the **United Nations**.

• The **People's Republic of China (PRC)** took over the permanent seat in **1971**. Previously, the seat was held by the **Republic of China (ROC)**, which is now based in **Taiwan**, following **UN General Assembly Resolution 2758**.

• The **BRICS** group held its first formal summit in **Yekaterinburg**, **Russia**, in **2009**. The acronym was coined by **Jim O'Neill** of **Goldman Sachs** in **2001** to describe the fast-growing economies that would dominate the global market by **2050**.

questions.question: The Chagos Archipelago is a disputed territory between ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**United Kingdom and Mauritius**__.

**__Key Points__**

__

• The **Chagos Archipelago** is a group of **seven atolls** comprising more than **60 individual tropical islands** in the **Indian Ocean**, located about **500 kilometres** south of the **Maldives** archipelago.

• The sovereignty of the **Chagos Archipelago** has been a long-standing point of contention between the **United Kingdom** and **Mauritius** since the **1960s**.

• The dispute began in **1965**, when the **United Kingdom** decided to excise the **Chagos Archipelago** from the colony of **Mauritius** to create the **British Indian Ocean Territory (BIOT)**, just three years before **Mauritius** gained independence in **1968**.

• **Mauritius** has consistently maintained that the detachment of the islands was a violation of **United Nations Resolution 1514**, which prohibits the disruption of the territorial integrity of colonies prior to their independence.

• In a landmark development in **October 2024**, the **United Kingdom** and **Mauritius** reached a political agreement where the **UK** agreed to transfer sovereignty of the **Chagos Archipelago** to **Mauritius**, effectively resolving the decades-old dispute.

**Additional Information__**

__

• **Diego Garcia**: This is the largest island in the **Chagos Archipelago** and is home to a strategically vital **United Kingdom-United States military base**. The base plays a critical role in **regional security** and global military operations in the **Indo-Pacific** and **Middle East**.

• **Expulsion of Chagossians**: Between **1967** and **1973**, the **United Kingdom** government forcibly removed the entire native population, known as the **Chagossians** or **Ilois**, to **Mauritius** and the **Seychelles** to facilitate the construction of the military base on **Diego Garcia**.

• **ICJ Advisory Opinion (2019)**: The **International Court of Justice (ICJ)** in **The Hague** issued an advisory opinion in **February 2019**, stating that the process of decolonization of **Mauritius** was not lawfully completed and that the **United Kingdom** is under an obligation to end its administration of the **Chagos Archipelago** as rapidly as possible.

• **UN General Assembly Resolution**: Following the **ICJ** ruling, the **United Nations General Assembly** passed a resolution in **May 2019** with an overwhelming majority, demanding that the **UK** withdraw its colonial administration from the islands within **six months**.

• **ITLOS Ruling**: In **2021**, the **International Tribunal for the Law of the Sea (ITLOS)** also ruled that the **United Kingdom** has no sovereignty over the **Chagos Archipelago** and criticized its failure to return the territory to **Mauritius**.

**Important Points__**

• **The 2024 Treaty Details**: Under the historic **2024 agreement**, while **Mauritius** will now hold sovereignty over the entire archipelago, the **United Kingdom** will be authorized to exercise the sovereign rights of **Mauritius** in respect of **Diego Garcia** for an initial period of **99 years**.

• **Resettlement Rights**: The agreement includes a **trust fund** and financial support to enable **Mauritius** to implement a programme of resettlement for the **Chagossian** people on islands other than **Diego Garcia**.

• **Strategic Importance**: The resolution of this dispute is seen as a major step in securing the long-term future of the **Diego Garcia** base while upholding **international law** and completing the **decolonization** process in the **Indian Ocean**.

• **Environmental Protection**: The **Chagos Archipelago** is home to some of the world's cleanest **coral reefs** and diverse marine life; the new agreement ensures continued **environmental cooperation** between the two nations.
</ul

questions.question: What is the troposphere?

options.text: The highest layer of the atmosphere
The lowest layer of the atmosphere
The middle layer of the atmosphere
The outermost layer of the atmosphere

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The lowest layer of the atmosphere**__

**__Key Points__**
__

• The **troposphere** is the **lowest layer** of Earth's atmosphere, starting at the **Earth's surface** and extending upwards.

• It contains approximately **75% to 80%** of the atmosphere's total mass and nearly all of its **water vapor** and **aerosols**.

• The height of the troposphere varies depending on the **latitude**; it is about **18 km** thick at the **equator** and about **8 km** thick at the **poles**.

• Almost all **weather phenomena**, including clouds, rain, and snow, occur in this layer because it holds the majority of the atmosphere's moisture.

• In the troposphere, the **temperature decreases** as altitude increases, which is why mountain tops are often covered in snow even in summer.

**Additional Information__**

• The boundary that separates the troposphere from the layer above it is called the **tropopause**.

• The **stratosphere** lies above the troposphere and contains the **ozone layer**, which absorbs and scatters solar **ultraviolet (UV) radiation**.

• The **mesosphere** is the middle layer where most **meteors** burn up upon entering the atmosphere.

• The **thermosphere** is the layer where the **International Space Station** orbits and where **auroras** (Northern and Southern Lights) occur.

• The **exosphere** is the **outermost layer** of the atmosphere, which gradually fades into the vacuum of **outer space**.
</ul

• The site was designated as a **UNESCO World Heritage Site** in **1986** because of its unique artistic creation and historical significance. The sculptures depict various aspects of daily life, mythical stories, and symbolic values.

• The **Brihadeshwara Temple**, located in **Thanjavur, Tamil Nadu**, was built by **Raja Raja Chola I** in the **11th century**. While it is a **UNESCO World Heritage Site**, it is known for its **Dravidian architecture** and massive **Vimana**, not primarily for erotic sculptures. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***

• The **Sun Temple, Konark**, located in **Odisha**, was built by **King Narasimhadeva I** of the **Eastern Ganga Dynasty** in the **13th century**. It is a **UNESCO World Heritage Site** shaped like a giant chariot, but the primary theme is the **Sun God, Surya**. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***

• The **Meenakshi Temple** is a historic Hindu temple located on the southern bank of the **Vaigai River** in the temple city of **Madurai, Tamil Nadu**. It is dedicated to **Goddess Meenakshi** (Parvati) and **Lord Sundareswarar** (Shiva). Although it is an architectural marvel, it is not currently a **UNESCO World Heritage Site**. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

**Additional Information__**

• **Architectural Style:** The Khajuraho temples are built in the **Nagara style**, characterized by a beehive-shaped tower called a **Shikhara**. The temples are made of **sandstone**, and the blocks were put together with **mortise and tenon joints**, held in place by gravity.

• **The Erotic Art:** The erotic sculptures, often called **Mithuna**, represent about **10%** of the total carvings on the temple walls. These are interpreted as a celebration of **Kama** (desire), which is one of the four goals of human life (**Purusharthas**) in Hindu philosophy, alongside **Dharma**, **Artha**, and **Moksha**.

• **Religious Diversity:** The site is unique because it contains both **Hindu** and **Jain** temples in close proximity, indicating a high level of **religious tolerance** and harmony during the **Chandela rule**.

• **Kandariya Mahadeva Temple:** This is the largest and most ornate temple in the Khajuraho complex. It is dedicated to **Lord Shiva** and is decorated with more than **800 sculptures** depicting gods, goddesses, musicians, and erotic couples.

• **Rediscovery:** After the decline of the **Chandela dynasty** in the **13th century**, the temples were largely forgotten and covered by dense forests. They were rediscovered by a **British engineer** named **T.S. Burt** in **1838**.

**Important Points__**

• **Number of Temples:** Historical records suggest that there were originally **85 temples** spread over **20 square kilometers**. Today, only about **25 temples** remain in a reasonable state of preservation.

• **Geographical Location:** The temples are situated in the **Vindhya Mountain Range** in central India. The nearest major city is **Jhansi**, and the site is a major hub for **cultural tourism** in **Madhya Pradesh**.

• **Khajuraho Dance Festival:** Every year in **February or March**, the **Madhya Pradesh Kala Parishad** organizes a week-long festival of **classical Indian dances** (like **Kathak**, **Bharatanatyam**, and **Odissi**) against the spectacular backdrop of the **Chitragupta** and **Vishwanatha** temples.

• **Classification:** The temples are generally divided into three geographical groups: the **Western Group** (most famous), the **Eastern Group**, and the **Southern Group**. The **Lakshmana Temple** and **Matangeshvara Temple** are other significant structures within these groups.

questions.question: The smallest set of, sum of three consecutive natural numbers is equal to the sum of two whole numbers, and one of the whole numbers is 0. Which of the following sets represents the three natural number?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Smallest consecutive natural numbers start from 1.

Set: 1, 2, 3 → Sum = 1 + 2 + 3 = 6.

Whole numbers: 0 and 6 → Sum = 0 + 6 = 6.

The condition is satisfied with the smallest possible natural numbers.

**∴ The correct answer is 1, 2, 3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Three consecutive natural numbers. One whole number is 0.

**Formula Used:** Sum of consecutive numbers = n + (n + 1) + (n + 2) = 3n + 3.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a7a76d7843dab8b308c48f5556bc8a5eea0c0ce762457d87585968988b64da96.png] 

⇒ Let the three consecutive natural numbers be n, n + 1, and n + 2.

⇒ Sum = n + (n + 1) + (n + 2) = 3n + 3.

⇒ Let the two whole numbers be W₁ and W₂.

⇒ Given W₁ = 0, so Sum = 0 + W₂ = W₂.

⇒ 3n + 3 = W₂.

⇒ Since n must be a natural number (n ≥ 1), the smallest value is n = 1.

⇒ Smallest set = {1, 1 + 1, 1 + 2} = {1, 2, 3}.

**∴ The correct answer is 1, 2, 3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Natural Numbers

Natural numbers are counting numbers starting from 1, 2, 3, up to infinity (∞).

Whole Numbers

Whole numbers include all natural numbers and the number zero (0, 1, 2, 3...).

Consecutive Numbers

Consecutive numbers follow each other in order, with a common difference of 1 between each term.

questions.question: The set of whole numbers consists of all natural numbers along with which additional number?
questions.solution:

Natural numbers (N) start from 1: {1, 2, 3, ...}.

Whole numbers (W) start from 0: {0, 1, 2, 3, ...}.

Therefore, Whole numbers = Natural numbers + zero.

⇒ W − N = {0}

⇒ Thus, the set of whole numbers consists of all natural numbers along with zero.

**∴ The correct answer is zero.**

**__Additional Information__**

Integers (Z)

Integers include all whole numbers and their negative counterparts: {..., −3, −2, −1, 0, 1, 2, 3, ...}.

Smallest Numbers

The smallest natural number is 1, whereas the smallest whole number is 0.

Rational Numbers

Every whole number is a rational number because it can be written as p/1, where p is the whole number.</p

questions.question: What is the decimal form of 7/8?

To convert a fraction with denominator 8 to a decimal, multiply both parts by 125 to make the denominator 1000.

⇒ 60 ÷ 8 = 0.07 (Remainder = 4)

⇒ 40 ÷ 8 = 0.005 (Remainder = 0)

⇒ Decimal value = 0.8 + 0.07 + 0.005 = 0.875

**∴ The correct answer is 0.875.**

**__Additional Information__**

Terminating Decimals

A fraction in its simplest form results in a terminating decimal if the prime factors of the denominator are only 2 and 5. Since 8 = 2³, 7/8 is a terminating decimal.

Reciprocal of 8

The decimal value of 1/8 is 0.125. To find 7/8, simply calculate 7 × 0.125 = 0.875.

questions.question: The average age of 5 friends is 24 years. If two new friends join the group, with one aged 25 years and another aged 30 years, what will be the new average age of the expanded group?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Initial average of **5 friends** = 24 years.

Deviation of new friends from 24: (25 − 24) = **+1** and (30 − 24) = **+6**.

Total net deviation = +1 + 6 = **+7**.

Average deviation for **7 friends** = +7 ÷ 7 = **+1**.

New average = 24 + 1 = 25 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 25 years.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial number of friends = 5

Initial average age = 24 years

Ages of 2 new friends = 25 years and 30 years

**Formula Used:**

Average = Sum of all observations ÷ Total number of observations

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f2c0757c5fd91eefec0b508eb9938ab91783b7011f1e4344fea039281b92e25a.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total age of 5 friends = 5 × 24 = 120 years

⇒ Total age of 7 friends = 120 + 25 + 30

⇒ Total age of 7 friends = 175 years

⇒ New average age = 175 ÷ 7

⇒ New average age = 25 years

**∴ The correct answer is 25 years.**

**__Additional Information__**

Average Concept

The average is the central value of a set of data, calculated by dividing the **sum of values** by the **number of values**.

Effect of New Entry

If a new value is **greater** than the current average, the average **increases**. If it is **smaller**, the average **decreases**.

Weighted Average

When combining two groups with different averages, the combined average is (n₁A₁ + n₂A₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).</p

questions.question: In a class, 60% of the students are boys and the rest are girls. If 40% of the boys and 50% of the girls passed a test, what percentage of the total students passed the test?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**44%**__

 __Shortcut Trick__

Assume **Total Students** = 100.

**Boys** = 60 and **Girls** = 40.

**Passed Boys** = 40% of 60 = 24.

**Passed Girls** = 50% of 40 = 20.

**Total Passed** = 24 + 20 = 44.

**∴ The correct answer is 44%.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Percentage of **Boys** = 60%

Percentage of **Girls** = 100% − 60% = 40%

Pass rate of **Boys** = 40%

Pass rate of **Girls** = 50%

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4c9219aacdf9ccf49eccb9ecbfc3605f972200764e6b1598c497b17f5e9686a1.png] 

⇒ Let the **Total Students** in the class be 100.

⇒ Number of **Boys** = 60% of 100 = 60.

⇒ Number of **Girls** = 100 − 60 = 40.

⇒ Number of **Boys who passed** = 40% of 60 = (40/100) × 60 = 24.

⇒ Number of **Girls who passed** = 50% of 40 = (50/100) × 40 = 20.

⇒ **Total students who passed** = 24 + 20 = 44.

⇒ **Total pass percentage** = (44/100) × 100 = 44%.

**∴ The correct answer is 44%.**

**__Additional Information__**

Weighted Average Method

The total pass percentage can be calculated using the weighted average formula: Total Pass % = (n₁p₁ + n₂p₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂), where n is the quantity and p is the percentage.

Percentage of a Quantity

To find the percentage of a specific number, multiply the number by the percentage value and divide by 100. Formula: Value = (Percentage × Total) ÷ 100.

Base Value Assumption

In percentage problems where absolute numbers are not given, assuming the total base value as 100 simplifies calculations significantly.</p

questions.question: A scholar was asked to find the arithmetic mean of the numbers 4, 11, 7, 9, 16, 13, 8, 19, 18, 21, 12 and x. He found the mean to be 12. What should be the number in place of x?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Assume the mean 12 is the balance point for all numbers.

Calculate net deviation of the 11 given numbers from 12:

(−8) + (−1) + (−5) + (−3) + 4 + 1 + (−4) + 7 + 6 + 9 + 0 = +6

To maintain the mean at 12, the 12th number x must compensate for the +6 deviation.

x = 12 − 6 = 6

**∴ The correct answer is 6.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Numbers = 4, 11, 7, 9, 16, 13, 8, 19, 18, 21, 12, x | Total count (n) = 12 | Arithmetic Mean = 12

**Formula Used:** Arithmetic Mean = Sum of observations ÷ Number of observations

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/77b14e0015f05d6bed32d2bbc9cddad0ccbb71d3e8e2c99a445aa6aa1a14ff60.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Sum of 11 numbers = 4 + 11 + 7 + 9 + 16 + 13 + 8 + 19 + 18 + 21 + 12 = 138

⇒ Total Sum of 12 numbers = 138 + x

⇒ Mean = (138 + x) ÷ 12

⇒ 12 = (138 + x) ÷ 12

⇒ 138 + x = 12 × 12

⇒ 138 + x = 144

⇒ x = 144 − 138

⇒ x = 6

**∴ The correct answer is 6.**

**__Additional Information__**

Arithmetic Mean

It is the average of a set of numerical values, calculated by adding them together and dividing by the count of those values.

Sum of Deviations

The algebraic sum of the deviations of a set of observations from their arithmetic mean is always zero.

Effect of Operations on Mean

If each observation in a data set is increased, decreased, multiplied, or divided by a constant k, the mean also changes by the same operation with k.</p

questions.question: A man covers a certain distance by car in 5 hours. If he increases his speed by 12 km/h, he takes one hour less to cover the same distance. What is the original speed of the car?

 __Shortcut Trick__

Since **distance is constant**, the **speed ratio** is the inverse of the **time ratio**.

Time ratio = 5 : 4

Speed ratio = 4 : 5

Difference in speed units = 5 − 4 = 1 unit

1 unit → 12 km/h

Original speed (4 units) = 4 × 12 = 48 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 48 km/h.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Original time = 5 h, New time = 4 h, Speed increase = 12 km/h

⇒ Distance = (S + 12) × 4

⇒ 5S = 4S + 48

⇒ 5S − 4S = 48

⇒ S = 48 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 48 km/h.**

**__Additional Information__**

Inverse Proportion Rule

When distance is constant, speed (S) is inversely proportional to time (T). Formula: S₁/S₂ = T₂/T₁.

Average Speed

For a journey with two equal distances at speeds x and y, Average Speed = 2xy ÷ (x + y).

Unit Conversion

questions.question: In a college, the ratio of the number of boys to girls is 8 : 5. If there are 180 girls, the total number of students in the college is:

Ratio of Boys : Girls = 8 : 5

Total Ratio parts = 8 + 5 = 13 units

Given: 5 units (Girls) = 180

1 unit = 180 ÷ 5 = 36

Total students = 13 units × 36 = 468

**∴ The correct answer is 468.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Ratio of Boys to Girls = 8 : 5

Number of Girls = 180

**Formula Used:**

Total Students = (Sum of Ratio Parts) × (Value of 1 Ratio Unit)

**Calculations:**

Let the number of boys and girls be 8x and 5x respectively.

⇒ Number of girls = 5x = 180

⇒ x = 180 ÷ 5

⇒ x = 36

⇒ Total number of students = Boys + Girls

⇒ Total students = 8x + 5x = 13x

⇒ Total students = 13 × 36

⇒ Total students = 468

**∴ The correct answer is 468.**

**__Additional Information__**

Ratio Sum Property

If a total quantity is divided in the ratio a : b, the total parts are (a + b). Each part can be found as [a/(a+b)] × Total or [b/(a+b)] × Total.

Unitary Method in Ratios

The value of one ratio unit is constant for all parts of that specific ratio. Once 1 unit is found, any component or the total can be calculated by multiplication.

Percentage Composition

To find the percentage of a part in a ratio a : b, use the formula: [a ÷ (a + b)] × 100.</p

questions.question: A person takes 2 hours to travel a certain distance by scooter. Returning over the same distance, he increases his speed by 10 km/h and takes 1.6 hours. What was his original speed?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of Time (T₁ : T₂) = 2 : 1.6 = 20 : 16 = 5 : 4

Since distance is constant, Speed ratio is inverse of Time ratio ⇒ S₁ : S₂ = 4 : 5

Speed increase = 5 − 4 = 1 unit. Given, 1 unit = 10 km/h.

Original Speed (S₁) = 4 units = 4 × 10 = 40 km/h.

**∴ The correct answer is 40 km/h.**

**Formula Used:**

Distance = Speed × Time

**Calculations:**

Let the original speed be S km/h.

⇒ Distance = Original Speed × Original Time = S × 2

⇒ Returning Distance = (S + 10) × 1.6

Since the distance is the same:

⇒ 2S = 1.6(S + 10)

⇒ 2S = 1.6S + 16

⇒ 2S − 1.6S = 16

⇒ 0.4S = 16

⇒ S = 16 ÷ 0.4

⇒ S = 160 ÷ 4 = 40 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 40 km/h.**

Speed, Distance, and Time Relation

The fundamental formula is Distance = Speed × Time. When distance is constant, speed and time are inversely proportional (S₁/S₂ = T₂/T₁).

Average Speed for Constant Distance

If a person travels equal distances at speeds S₁ and S₂, the average speed for the whole journey is (2 × S₁ × S₂) ÷ (S₁ + S₂).

To convert speed from km/h to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert from m/s to km/h, multiply by 18/5.</p

questions.question: A triangle has angles in the ratio 2:3:4. What are the angles?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of angles = 2 : 3 : 4

Total units = 2 + 3 + 4 = 9 units

Since total angle sum is 180°, 9 units = 180°

1 unit = 180° ÷ 9 = 20°

Angles are (2 × 20°), (3 × 20°), (4 × 20°) = 40°, 60°, 80°

**∴ The correct answer is 40°, 60°, 80°.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Ratio of angles = 2 : 3 : 4

**Formula Used:**

Sum of interior angles of a triangle = 180°

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/956aa8ceb0bfad9a0a5276c901b5fcd926959ed460b9a7ad0cf36116183f06d0.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the three angles of the triangle be 2x, 3x, and 4x.

⇒ According to the angle sum property:

⇒ 2x + 3x + 4x = 180°

⇒ 9x = 180°

⇒ x = 180° ÷ 9

⇒ x = 20°

⇒ First angle = 2x = 2 × 20° = 40°

⇒ Second angle = 3x = 3 × 20° = 60°

⇒ Third angle = 4x = 4 × 20° = 80°

**∴ The correct answer is 40°, 60°, 80°.**

**__Additional Information__**

Angle Sum Property

The sum of all internal angles of any triangle is always 180° or π radians.

Exterior Angle Theorem

The exterior angle of a triangle is equal to the sum of its two opposite interior angles.

Classification by Angles

Triangles are Acute (all angles 90°).

Polygon Angle Sum Formula

Sum of interior angles of an n-sided polygon is given by (n − 2) × 180°.</p

questions.question: A cone has a slant height of 13 cm and a vertical height of 5 cm. What is the radius of the base?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The relationship between vertical height (h), radius (r), and slant height (l) of a cone forms a right-angled triangle.

Identify the standard Pythagorean triplet where the hypotenuse is 13 and one side is 5.

The triplet (5, 12, 13) satisfies the condition: 5² + 12² = 13².

Since height h = 5 cm and slant height l = 13 cm, the radius r must be 12 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 12 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Slant height (l) = 13 cm

Vertical height (h) = 5 cm

**Formula:**

In a right circular cone, the slant height is given by: l² = r² + h²

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d78f2d97f0f20568df67808d7f1e05e8ac3b762bb9084c96ac1eb8b459f21035.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 13² = r² + 5²

⇒ 169 = r² + 25

⇒ r² = 169 − 25

⇒ r² = 144

⇒ r = √144

⇒ r = 12 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 12 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Volume of a Cone

The volume (V) is one-third the volume of a cylinder with the same base and height: V = (1/3) × πr²h.

Curved Surface Area (CSA)

The area of the curved part of the cone is given by: CSA = π × r × l.

Total Surface Area (TSA)

The sum of the base area and the curved surface area: TSA = πr² + πrl = πr(r + l).

Common Pythagorean Triplets

Frequently used triplets in exams include (3, 4, 5), (5, 12, 13), (8, 15, 17), and (7, 24, 25).</p
